pages.actualObservation: Title reads Lecture Number 59, Mobile Robot Demonstration. Printed footer 1.
Learning outcomes roadmap: AMR architecture, differential drive, odometry/PID, EKF, SLAM/AMCL/Nav2, planning and YOLOv8. Bottom line nearly touches footer; readable. No new implementation detail.
Contents roadmap only: traditional/AI comparison, AMR, differential drive, motion model and demonstration.

Five-row comparison distinguishes sensor-driven inference and classical model/control methods; explicitly says this robot integrates YOLOv8n with classical robotics. Do not infer AI replaces PID or that all classical robots lack perception.

AMR definition does not require continuous human intervention. All five roles inspected: perception, localization, planning, navigation and adaptive decision making. Robot photo is an overview, not a component-labelled proof.

Front/side drawings distinguish two driven wheels and passive caster. Equal signed wheel speeds give straight motion; opposite signs require equal magnitudes to yield pure in-place rotation under the next page equations. Simplicity and indoor mapping/navigation uses are qualitative.

Read exact v=r(omega_R+omega_L)/2 and omega=r(omega_R-omega_L)/L. r is common radius, L full wheel separation. Diagram distinguishes wheel angular/linear rates and body rates. Positive convention follows right-minus-left; added derivations explicitly assume no slip and equal radii.

Demonstration uses Jetson Orin Nano, Arduino Mega2560, RPLidar and RealSense D435i RGB/depth/IMU. ROS2 Humble, SLAM Toolbox, AMCL, Nav2, robot_localization EKF, YOLOv8n named. Hardware-validation statement is source-reported, not reproduced here.

System-layer diagram read in full: sensors to EKF/perception/localization; SLAM/AMCL to navigation; YOLOv8 arrow into costmap; velocity to Arduino/controller/drivers/motors. Jetson, ROS2 Humble and RViz2 boxes are infrastructure. Sequential planner/local/BT/costmap arrows are conceptual, not a launch graph or scheduling proof.

Photo arrows and all seven hardware boxes read: RPLidar planar360 scans; D435i RGB/depth/IMU; Jetson compute; Arduino low-level control/encoder interface; Cytron MDD10A drive signals; wheel encoder rotation; battery power. No exact voltage/current rating printed.

Wheel rotation→encoder pulses→wheel displacement→pose(x,y,theta). Quadrature encoders and differential kinematics. Odometry continuous but accumulates slip/terrain drift. Encoder counts per revolution, gearing and decode multiplier not supplied.

PID objectives include tracking, steady/transient error, varying load and stability; desired→PID→PWM→motor→encoder feedback diagram. Table P present error, I accumulated error, D overshoot/stability role. No gains, sample rate, saturation/antiwindup or performance guarantee supplied.

Frame table: map global, odom continuous, base_link robot body, laser LiDAR, camera_link RGB-D. Diagram clearly map→odom→base_link, lower sensor-box arrow is abbreviated and does not provide numeric extrinsics. TF maintains configured spatial relationships, not automatic calibration.

Wheel odometry+IMU+RPLidar scan schematic feeds EKF→filtered pose. Text gives slip drift, IMU long-term drift and uncertainty. No message types, measurement model, scan-to-pose frontend or noise covariances printed, so cannot infer direct raw-scan subscription or guaranteed improvement.

LiDAR360 range/plane versus RGB-D depth/off-plane/narrower field comparison. Actual legend: magenta lethal, cyan inscribed, reddish high cost, purple low cost, gray free. LiDAR+depth→local costmap→obstacle representation. Colours are source visualization, not universal RGB constants or a full collision certificate.

SLAM jointly builds unknown-environment map and pose; this implementation uses 2D occupancy grid and planar pose(x,y,theta), loop closure, incremental exploration and navigation map. Do not universalize all SLAM to2D.

Teleoperate, collect scans, EKF-filtered odometry, generate/update grid, save map for AMCL/Nav2. Initial scan screenshot and completed grid screenshot differ; saved map reused later. Static images do not establish convergence error or runtime.

AMCL prebuilt-map particle filter, multiple pose hypotheses, compare incoming scans, update pose; outputs position/orientation/confidence. Workflow saved map+scan→particles→scan comparison→probability update→pose. No particle count or actual confidence statistic printed.
Goal pose includes x,y,theta. Screenshot distinguishes 2D Pose Estimate from 2D Goal Pose; green target arrow has direction. Select goal→plan→move→reached. Goal tolerance is not supplied.

Global planning uses occupancy grid, current pose+goal, static obstacles, replans on change, long-range route. Optimal/collision-free/smooth language lacks algorithm/cost/footprint/uncertainty definitions; not an unconditional guarantee.

Local planning tracks global route, reacts to new obstacles and generates feasible linear/angular velocity commands. Label arrows point to longer green global path and shorter local path. No named plugin/tuning supplied; distinguish desired velocity from wheel PWM.

ROS component table: node called independent executable, topic asynchronous, service request-response, action long-running navigation, TF transforms. Concept diagram processing→navigation and motor controller. No actual node/process graph, message names or executable code printed.

Nav2 table: Planner Server global path, Controller Server trajectory tracking, BT Navigator behavior, costmaps obstacle info, recovery behaviors failures. Right diagram behavior server in sequence is conceptual. Implementation uses saved map, AMCL, filtered odom, LiDAR+depth. No server plugin or launch configuration.

YOLOv8 RGB detection, aligned depth for distance, annotated images, semantic awareness on Jetson. Pipeline image→network→boxes→class→confidence. Chair box score0.83 visibly printed; score alone not a calibrated probability or metric depth. No source inference code/model execution supplied.

Simulation models robot/environment kinematics/dynamics/sensors/interactions and allows same ROS2 stack. Listed outputs LiDAR,RGB-D,IMU,odom, maps/plans. Simulation is useful evidence, not proof of identical hardware performance.

Table maps robot model to URDF/Xacro physical properties, environment to obstacles/boundaries, sensors to virtual data, motion to differential dynamics, navigation to SLAM/localization/planning/control. Right flow repeats Robot Decision twice; no additional algorithm inferred from duplicate label.

Map-generation static video frame shows Gazebo world and RViz display, teleop caption and playback speed4x. Centre pane labelled Terminal is visibly a property/entity panel, so do not infer exact terminal command. No temporal execution or timing measured.
Simulation static video frame shows virtual camera image, Gazebo world and RViz map; caption preconfigured world/map, playback3x. No code or time-resolved recording embedded in page.

Hardware demonstration static frame shows real corridor chair/backpack/robot, RViz map and annotation Robot Initialized and Map Loaded. Playback3.25x is not measured robot speed or a hard-real-time deadline.
Summary repeats differential drive, odometry/PID, multisensor fusion, SLAM/AMCL/Nav2 and YOLOv8n. Reported simulation/hardware validation remains distinct from this author inspection.

Bibliography names Siegwart/Nourbakhsh and NVIDIA, AI-Geniuses GitHub profile, Nav2, SLAM Toolbox, ROS2 Humble, Gazebo, RealSense and RPLidar documentation. No unique original executable package/commit identified.
Closing thank-you only. Footer32.
